label: rejected

evidence.V1: Silhouette reads as a gable roof from three-quarter and silhouette; front reads as a sloped tiled roof with timber eave; top shows ridge + courses clearly.
evidence.V2: Big (two slopes + gable) and medium (5 tile courses, ridge roll, timber eave beam) present, but no small tier (no pegs, battens, bargeboard detail) and the gable triangle is one large empty plane.
evidence.V3: Courses are uniform straight slabs and the gable is a plain flat triangle; reads close to a primitive prism with stripes rather than a confidently stylised roof (no sag, overhang flare or chunky barge boards).
evidence.V4: Eave beam and ridge roll have soft chamfers, but tile-course lower edges read thin/razor in the shingles close-up and the gable panel edge meets the slope with a hard, unbevelled junction.
evidence.V5: No pinches or seams; faint horizontal streaking on the ridge roll in ridge close-up (likely overlap of ridge over top course, cross_shell_overlaps 210); otherwise clean gradients.
evidence.V6: Stone hue in 3 values (alternating light/mid course + darker ridge) plus timber secondary; disciplined across granite/brick/sandstone colourways.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material and chamfers match, but the timber gable reads near-black/very dark in studio light and no cream plaster or gold accents; slightly off the bright kit look.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling pass (iou 1.0).

artifacts: faint horizontal streaking on ridge roll (possible overlap/z-fight with top course)
top_fixes: Break up the gable end: add barge boards, cream plaster infill with timber cross-beams or a small vent so the large flat triangle has medium/small detail
Give tile course lower edges a visible chamfer/thickness lip and slight overhang at the gable so the courses catch light
Lift the gable timber value so it does not read near-black; check ridge-roll overlap for streaking
